text: Building permits, Toledo 1537: Cathedral extension approved for construction outside of time but within city limits. Foundation stones dated simultaneously to all centuries. Architect listed as The Department of Necessary Impossibilities.

Botanical survey, Amazon Basin: Tree ring analysis from 800yearold cecropia shows growth spurts during nuclear tests, 19451963. Tree predates European contact. Rings contain trace amounts of strontium90 from future atmospheric fallout.

Postal records, Morocco 1456: Letter delivered to recipient who died three years before sender was born. Postmark authenticated by guild of scribes. Reply was sent same day, arrived forty years early.

Census data, Northern England 1851: Household registry lists family of seven living in singleroom cottage with fourteen bedrooms. Enumerator's marginal note: Rooms exist only on Thursdays. Property tax assessed accordingly.

Archaeological excavation, Çatalhöyük 6500 BCE: Obsidian blade found with microscopic serial number etched in Latin script. Blade composition matches Anatolian volcanic glass. Serial format corresponds to 1970s manufacturing standards.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1789: Patient admitted with symptoms of drowning in desert. Lungs contained saltwater, sand, and fragments of ships that wouldn't be built for sixty years. Recovery was complete by morning.

Wildlife census, Yellowstone 1923: Pack of wolves documented hunting in formation that spells out coordinates in base16. Location corresponds to den site that won't exist until park expansion of 1978. Wolves extinct in region since 1926.

Seismic records, California 1906: Earthquake tremors recorded in perfect iambic pentameter. Duration exactly matches reading time of sonnet discovered in Pompeii ruins. Sonnet predicts San Francisco fire with geological precision.

Meteorological station, Antarctic Peninsula 1957: Wind patterns formed complete musical score over sixhour period. Composition matched symphony that premiered in Vienna three months later. Composer had never seen weather data.

Personal diary, merchant's daughter, Florence 1634: The plague doctor's mask contained seventeen different faces today. Father says I have fever dreams but the baker's son drew the same seventeen faces without seeing my journal.

Archaeological survey, Mesopotamia 2400 BCE: USB drive recovered with cuneiform adapter still attached. Contains inventory of ziggurats not yet constructed. Drive formatted in Sumerian base60. Data corrupted by centuries of prayer.

Hospital records, St. Bartholomew's London 1665: Patient admitted with symptoms of temporal displacement. Complained of missing the internet. Spoke fluent English with accent that won't develop until Australian colonization.

Geological survey, Triassic period 210 million BCE: Dinosaur trackways form perfect hexagonal pattern spanning 12 kilometers. Pattern matches urban street grid of Philadelphia, 1682 city plan. Tracks predate William Penn by 210 million year

Census enumeration, rural Vermont 1820: Household listed family of four plus the Tuesday that got lost. Enumerator noted Tuesday responds to questions, pays taxes, owns property deed dated for day that never occurred.

Weather station data, Antarctica 1957: Barometric readings spell out recipe for grandmother's cookies in Morse code. No grandmother stationed at base. Recipe calls for ingredients that don't exist. Cookies taste exactly like childhood.
